heading: Application for Discover Graduate Program Greece — Technology
paragraphs: I am applying for the Technology stream of the Discover Graduate Program in Athens. The programme covers cyber security engineering, network engineering, virtualisation and automation, and application delivery and support, which is close to the direction I have been working in since I completed my Master's in Information Security. I am drawn to Vodafone because a telecoms operator runs some of the most exposed infrastructure there is, and because this programme rotates across several of the areas I want to build a career in rather than narrowing to one immediately. I would like to start somewhere the technology is the business.

On the security side, my day-to-day work is triage. In my current IT support role I investigate four or five suspicious emails a day, check sender and link domains for impersonation, document what I find and warn colleagues about recurring tactics. For my Master's I designed a phishing analysis prototype that mapped suspicious email indicators to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, then evaluated it against a mixture of suspicious and legitimate business emails to see where it broke down. That work taught me to treat false positives as the central problem in detection rather than an afterthought. For a security engineering team, the gain is someone who already works to that instinct and can explain why a detection fired.

The other areas in the programme are where most of my practical experience sits. I support around fifteen users across fifteen to twenty devices, working with Windows, Microsoft 365 and Azure, and I run the access request process through on-premises Active Directory, including time-limited permissions and the documentation that goes with them. I use Python and PowerShell for scripting and log analysis, and I built a local tool that maps Windows error codes to likely causes, so recurring faults can be investigated from a known starting point. My Master's modules included network security and critical infrastructure security. For a team covering network operations, virtualisation or automation, the gain is a graduate who can troubleshoot an endpoint, record the fix and then script the repeat.

I want to be direct about one requirement. The programme asks for proficiency in both English and Greek, and my Greek is not yet at a working level. I am willing to learn it and to commit to that alongside the programme from the start. I would rather raise it now than have it appear later in the process.
I would welcome the chance to discuss the programme further. My CV is attached, and I am happy to answer any questions about my experience, my studies or my projects.
